leads.summary: Existing Elsewhen migration symlink shadows the packaged plugin as untrusted
leads.consequence: On a dev-linked checkout where the Elsewhen migration has already created ~/.config/omarchy/plugins/omacom.elsewhen -> /usr/share/omarchy/shell/plugins/omacom.elsewhen, both scanners select that HOME symlink first. The same package is stamped third-party, not trusted, rather than being selected via XDG_DATA_DIRS. Its bar entry in stock shell.json still places it, but first-party APIs, declared capabilities and default enablement outside the bar are lost. Deleting only the migration-created symlink flips trust; the migration has no corresponding cleanup. PR #12871 removes creation for future migration runs but explicitly leaves existing installations' links alone.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus (informational item 3); published as N2 after coordinator read of migration and #12871 diff

leads.summary: The git installer refuses the personal override that XDG discovery now promises
leads.consequence: If a package supplies ID acme.example or omacom.example in an XDG root, `omarchy plugin add <git-url> --yes` validates a same-ID personal checkout but then `plugin_id_manifest` resolves the package from the catalog and exits with 'plugin id ... is already used by ...'. The target user directory is free, and a manually copied user checkout with that ID would be accepted and selected first, per docs/omarchy-shell.md:60. Consequently users cannot install the documented override via the normal git command; distinguish a same-ID packaged/bundled entry from a pre-existing personal target, then permit or explicitly document the exception. The personal-target collision is already guarded separately at add:140-144.
leads.triage: dropped: plugin add refusing any claimed ID is documented behaviour (manual/32-shell-plugins.md:44); a manual personal copy still overrides

leads.summary: The shipped shell plugin manual still says only checkout and user git directories exist
leads.consequence: Users following the manual are told packages are not a distribution option and only user git checkouts are discovered, missing the new documented XDG package workflow and omacom.* trust distinction. Update its origins/install/distribution sections along with docs/omarchy-shell.md:58-62, rather than telling readers to install a package by git clone.
leads.triage: verified by coordinator (manual/32-shell-plugins.md:7 lists two roots, PR does not touch manual/); published in documentation note

leads.summary: Coordinate with #13340 scanner record format before merging either PR
leads.consequence: Both PRs replace the scanner and parser on the same base. #13340 serializes the kind/source/manifest as JSONL, whereas this PR emits delimiter-framed records and recognizes the new `data` kind. Blindly keeping #13340's parser with this PR's scanner rejects every record; keeping #13340's scanner/parser loses XDG scanning and omacom trust; keeping this PR's parser reintroduces the record-framing vulnerability that #13340 explicitly fixes. Resolve both halves together and update the fixture to exercise package roots and encoded paths. The conflict is not evidence that #12872 itself introduced the pre-existing delimiter issue.
leads.triage: verified by coordinator (gh pr diff 13340: JSONL parser/scanner) and Opus self-check (parser accepts only firstparty/thirdparty); published in related-PR note

leads.summary: #12051's Atreyu package directory and omarchy.* trust contract do not compose with this scanner
leads.consequence: #12051 ships omarchy.atreyu under /usr/share/omarchy/plugins/<id>, a root #12872 does not search; even if that root were added as a data directory, #12872 rejects every data-origin omarchy.* plugin. After resolving the already-conflicting GitHub merge, keeping these rules makes the Atreyu entry in #12051's default bar layout unresolvable, and its own package/config fixture fails. Decide and implement a shared package root plus protected trusted namespace and precedence before landing both; this is a cross-PR integration conflict, not a defect in the current PR's stated omacom-only XDG contract.
leads.triage: dropped: #12051 is by the same author, and the Atreyu package-root integration is the author's own design question; not needed in this follow-up

leads.summary: #12981's external scanner would silently revert XDG discovery if used without adaptation
leads.consequence: #12981 replaces the inline rescan with scan-plugins.sh that accepts only firstPartyDir and pluginsDir. If that fix to Quickshell's inline-command execution is selected when resolving the overlapping rescan hunk, the shell never scans any XDG data roots although the CLI still does; the new discovery test's compositor-gated runtime half is required to notice it. Pass the data roots and distinct origin to the external script if adopting #12981. If instead keeping this PR's scanner, #12981's described inline-execution failures remain on affected machines.
leads.triage: verified by coordinator (gh pr diff 12981: scanProcess.command passes only firstPartyDir and pluginsDir); published in related-PR note

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified at `033a1496`:** both findings from the [initial review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12872#issuecomment-5776182188) remain resolved, and no regression was found in the five commits added since the [previous follow-up](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12872#issuecomment-5789505842). The rebase carried the earlier five commits over as identical patches. Two issues in the unchanged discovery code, a documentation note and a note on related open PRs follow; none of them changes the resolved findings.

| Prior finding | Status at `033a1496` |
|---|---|
| Unset `XDG_DATA_DIRS` reached Bash as the literal `"null"` | **Resolved.** [`PluginRegistry.qml`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/033a1496b26ba20b2c19882b34d825d71aaa848f/shell/services/PluginRegistry.qml#L704) still passes `Quickshell.env("XDG_DATA_DIRS") \|\| ""`. In native offscreen Quickshell 0.3.1 runs, the PR's runtime discovery test passed its unset case, and a registry scan with the variable unset read the default `/usr/share` root. |
| An old personal facade received its trusted replacement's manifest | **Resolved.** [`syncPluginApis()`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/033a1496b26ba20b2c19882b34d825d71aaa848f/shell/shell.qml#L922-L930) still prunes facades before assigning manifests. The callback-driven regression test passes, and moving the prune after the assignment makes it fail. The original native callback reproduction was not rerun. |

**Verified, new commits:**
- `11e429f6`: the single-map capability stamping matched the previous two-map version in 20,000 randomized selections.
- `a33b767a`, `667a63e2` and `026045c5`: the PR's regression tests for source-bound widget-registry, bar-entry and bar facades, stale asynchronous widget loads, failed widget replacements and disabled pending services pass, and each of 10 targeted mutants of the new guards makes them fail. Scenario runs against the previous head confirm the bar-facade and widget-load changes. Facade reuse is unchanged between rescans.
- `033a1496`: the new [catalog header](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/033a1496b26ba20b2c19882b34d825d71aaa848f/bin/omarchy-plugin-catalog#L7-L8) matches the script: HOME, then the active checkout, then ordered XDG data roots, with the first valid manifest per ID.

## Default install logs a reserved-ID rejection for every built-in

A standard install has `OMARCHY_PATH=/usr/share/omarchy`, so the default `/usr/share` data root is the same `shell/plugins` directory as the bundled root. The data-root pass then reaches every `omarchy.*` manifest again, and [the reserved-ID check](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/033a1496b26ba20b2c19882b34d825d71aaa848f/shell/services/PluginRegistry.qml#L594-L596) warns even when that ID was already selected from the bundled pass.

| Native simulation of the head tree | Selected plugins | "id is reserved" warnings per scan |
|---|---|---|
| Bundled root equals the default data root | 37, all trusted | 37 |
| Separate roots | Same 37 | 0 |

**Impact:** Plugin selection is unaffected, but every startup and rescan logs that each built-in was "rejected" although it loaded, which can mislead anyone debugging plugin discovery.

**Suggested change:** Skip a data root whose `omarchy/shell/plugins` directory is the bundled directory, for example `[[ ${data_dir%/}/omarchy/shell/plugins -ef $OMARCHY_PATH/shell/plugins ]] && continue` in the CLI catalog and the same test against `$0` in the shell scanner. Alternatively, warn only when the reserved ID was not already selected.

## Existing Elsewhen links keep the packaged plugin untrusted

On dev-linked installs, [`migrations/1790042972.sh`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/033a1496b26ba20b2c19882b34d825d71aaa848f/migrations/1790042972.sh#L14-L18) created `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/omacom.elsewhen` pointing at the packaged copy. With this PR the HOME entry still wins and is classified third-party. In a CLI catalog check with a synthetic `omacom.elsewhen` in a data root, it was selected with `firstParty: true` without the link and `firstParty: false` with it. This matches base behavior, and #12871 stops creating the link without removing existing ones.

**Impact:** Dev-linked systems that already ran the migration do not get the trusted packaged Elsewhen that XDG discovery now provides until the link is removed by hand.

**Suggested change:** Add a migration that removes the link only when it still points at `/usr/share/omarchy/shell/plugins/omacom.elsewhen`, leaving user-made copies alone.

**Documentation note:** Personal plugin directories now also accept adjacent `*.manifest.json` files (the base accepted only `<dir>/manifest.json`), while [`docs/omarchy-shell.md`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/033a1496b26ba20b2c19882b34d825d71aaa848f/docs/omarchy-shell.md#L60) describes adjacent `*.manifest.json` files only for bundled and data-directory plugins. `omarchy-plugin-remove` looks a plugin up by its directory name, so such an extra manifest's ID is not found. Either restrict the personal scan to `manifest.json` or document the behavior. [`manual/32-shell-plugins.md`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/033a1496b26ba20b2c19882b34d825d71aaa848f/manual/32-shell-plugins.md?plain=1#L7) still lists only the checkout and personal plugin roots.

**Related open PRs:** #13340 (JSONL scan records) and #12981 (external scan script) both rewrite the same scanner in `PluginRegistry.qml`, and neither scans data roots: the external script in #12981 takes only the bundled and personal roots, and the #13340 parser accepts only `firstparty` and `thirdparty` records. Whichever lands second needs this PR's data-root pass carried over, or the shell would stop discovering packaged plugins while the CLI catalog still lists them.

---
